chapter: Alma Hightower and other women musicians
title: What Howard was doing then: cleaning, not playing
summary: Howard says he was cleaning a basement and not playing at night then.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: Day jobs: musicians working outside music

blocks.x: No, I don't know of any others. I'n tell you what I was doing at that time.
Well, that's good, too.
Cleanin' out the basement of-- what's the name of that--?
Department store? Bullock's?
It wan't a department store.
Mmmmm.
It wadn't a department store-- yeah, I'se cleaning out the basement (chuckle).
I see. Now were you also working at night at that period, with your saxophone or cornet or something?
No.
No playing.
No playing.
Was Alma Hightower working any place then, at night, that you know of?
Not that I know of. No.
When did you have a opportunity to work with her, and hear her play? While in that same
period, or later?
Hey, Buddy, if I can think about-- you can help me, too, okay.
Okay.
--help me think about--you wouldn't know about it, though, 'cause you were too young.
Maybe. But what'a'ya mean, that period--?
Yeah, you wouldn't know, you couldn't think about it--wadn't no way in this world for you to think of it--because they had--what was that?
--Suzie--
Oh, What they had then, at that time, was anybody was just cleanin' up stores and things, that's--
Uh-huh.
That's why you wouldn't know anything about it.
